item.title: Your Agent's Shell Allowlist Is Bypassable
item.description: Every shipmates crew member runs shell commands, and before any of them runs it goes through a permission gate. The gate uses the same rule syntax as Claude Code settings, Bash(git status), Bash(rm *), Write(**/.claude/settings.json), merged from several layers: a fleet-wide deny list pushed from Fleet Command, per-persona policy files, project settings, and the Brig, which compiles shipmates’ fifteen “Ship’s Articles” into deny and ask rules. Deny beats ask, ask beats allow.

item.title: A 1 TB Test: Building a Memory Watchdog for go test
item.description:
On August 16th a server.test.exe from shipmates climbed to roughly 1 TB of commit charge on my Windows workstation. Windows Terminal, which was hosting several agent sessions in tabs, hard-faulted with E_OUTOFMEMORY and every one of those sessions died at the same moment. It wasn’t the first time either. An earlier one hit about 236 GB through an infinite filepath.Dir loop.

The machine has 128 GB of RAM. Commit charge doesn’t care, it’s backed by the page file, and Windows will happily let a process reserve-and-commit until the commit limit is gone. Then everything else on the desktop starts failing allocations too.
